item.title: AI Use Complicating Relationships and Dividing Friends, Families
item.description: AI is dividing people not just over what the technology can do, but what kind of future they want to live in.

item.title: South Africa’s Rand Faces Bleak August as Policy Stance Queried
item.description: August is historically the rand’s worst month, and traders expect this year to be no different as questions about the central bank’s policy stance add to seasonal woes for South Africa’s currency.

item.title: UK’s Markets Regulator Unveils Scope of Data Feed for Stocks
item.description: The UK Financial Conduct Authority unveiled how much data it will allow to be published on UK equities trading on Friday, a move that could encourage more activity on the London Stock Exchange.

item.title: Bain-Backed Dhoot Said to Plan $325 Million India IPO in August
item.description: Bain Capital-controlled Dhoot Transmission Ltd. is preparing to launch its initial public offering next month after completing investor roadshows, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: BOJ Data Point to Yen Intervention of Around $53 Billion
item.description: Japan likely spent around $53 billion intervening in the currency market on Thursday to prop up the yen, according to a Bloomberg analysis of central bank accounts.

item.title: Foreign Investors Shun Nigeria’s World-Beating Equities
item.description: Foreign investors shunned Nigerian stocks this year, choosing to focus on fixed-income assets, missing out on a 66% rally that made the market the world’s best performer.

item.title: Dollar Heads for Worst Week in Three Months as Fed Doubts Grow
item.description: The dollar headed for its worst week in three months on concerns the Federal Reserve won’t move forcefully enough to contain inflation.

item.title: Goldman Sees More South Africa Rating Upgrades on Strong Revenue
item.description: South Africa’s revenue outperformance puts the country on course for further credit-ratings upgrades over the next year, Goldman Sachs Group Inc. said.

item.title: Euro-Area Inflation Strengthens as US-Iran Strikes Boost Oil
item.description: Euro-area inflation picked up in July after the collapse of a US-Iran ceasefire boosted oil prices, reinforcing expectations that the European Central Bank will need to raise interest rates again.

item.title: China’s MiniMax and ByteDance Release Dueling AI Video Models
item.description: MiniMax Group Inc. and ByteDance Ltd. released updates to their dueling AI video generation models within hours of each other, underscoring the aggressive advances that have made China the leader over the US in the burgeoning arena.

item.title: Colombia to Hike Interest Rate in Last Petro-Era Meeting
item.description: Colombia’s central bank will likely lift its interest rate for the second straight month as inflation accelerates at the end of President Gustavo Petro’s term, which featured constant tension with the monetary authority.

item.title: Hong Kong’s Economy Slows More Than Forecast Despite AI Boom
item.description: Hong Kong’s economic growth slowed more than forecast last quarter, even as a global rush to invest in artificial intelligence turbocharges the city’s exports.

item.title: Taiwan’s Economy Clocks Fastest First-Half Growth Since 1976
item.description: Taiwan’s economy expanded at the fastest pace in some 50 years in the first half of 2026, data that should ease some concern among global investors about the outlook for AI.

item.title: Apple Leads Phone Revenues and Prices Up, Counterpoint Says
item.description: Apple Inc. led a 7% increase in global smartphone revenue over the June quarter, showing how rising prices are offsetting shrinking shipments, according to Counterpoint Research.

item.title: Griffin’s Move Offers AI Reprieve as Traders Eye More Blowouts
item.description: Billionaire Ken Griffin’s rescue of hedge fund Situational Awareness helped trigger a relief rally in global AI stocks, leaving traders debating if the worst is over or more blowouts are on the way.

item.title: DeepSeek Unveils Public Beta API for Flagship AI Model
item.description: China’s DeepSeek rolled out a public beta application programming interface, or API, for its flagship artificial intelligence model, V4 Flash, touting advancements in agentic abilities.

item.title: French Inflation Unexpectedly Accelerates on Services, Power
item.description: French inflation unexpectedly quickened this month, supporting the case for another European Central Bank interest-rate increase.

item.title: European Gas Prices Poised for Biggest Monthly Gain Since March
item.description: European natural gas prices are poised for their biggest monthly gain since March as the war in the Middle East continues to disrupt global energy supplies.

item.title: Kioxia’s Outlook Miss Clouds Optimism About Memory Chip Boom
item.description: Kioxia Holdings Corp. issued a disappointing earnings outlook after results missed expectations, a sign that an unprecedented AI-driven surge in flash memory prices may be moderating.

item.title: Sainsbury’s to Sell Argos Division for at Least £120 Million
item.description: J Sainsbury Plc agreed to sell its struggling Argos general merchandise unit to Swift Partners, a new company backed by retailers including former Co-op boss Richard Pennycook.

item.title: BP Starts Process for Potential Sale of North Sea Business
item.description: BP Plc said it’s starting a process to market its North Sea business for a potential sale, as part of a wider review of the oil major’s portfolio.

item.title: UK House Prices Edge Higher in July, Nationwide Says
item.description: UK house prices returned to growth in July, one of the country’s largest mortgage lenders said, as buyers weather higher borrowing costs linked to the Iran war better than expected.

item.title: Tokyo Court Says Shidax Tender Undervalued the Firm in Rare Case
item.description: The Tokyo District Court ruled that hospitality sector company Shidax Corp.’s tender offer in 2023 to go private undervalued its shares, in one of the still-rare cases in Japan of financial tussles between companies getting resolved by legal authorities.

item.title: FTSE Live: UK Stock Futures Rise, Pound Slips as Attention on Tech
item.description: FTSE Live: UK Stock Futures Rise, Pound Slips as Attention on Tech【原文：FTSE Live: UK Stock Futures Rise, Pound Slips as Attention on Tech】

item.title: Engie Lifts Profit Outlook on Cost Cuts, Currency Effects
item.description: French utility Engie SA raised its full-year profit forecast as it benefits from currency fluctuations, its huge acquisition in the UK, cost cuts and energy market volatility linked to the war in the Middle East, which helped mitigate a profit decline in the first six months of the year.

item.title: Saudi Ships Pivot from Red Sea Chokepoint for Rare Africa Trip
item.description: Six Saudi oil tankers are sailing away from the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint and appeared to be embarking on an unusual trip around Africa as threats from Houthi rebels upend shipping in the Red Sea.

item.title: Yen Strategists Parse IMF Rules for Clues to Japan’s Next Move
item.description: Strategists trying to figure out Japan’s next move on the yen are looking to the International Monetary Fund’s technical guidelines for clues.

item.title: Kenya Inflation Tops Target Midpoint a Third Month on Energy
item.description: Kenya’s annual inflation rate exceeded the midpoint of the central bank’s target range for a third month, as energy costs fueled price growth.

item.title: SNB Returns to Profit as Stocks Rally Offsets Gold Losses
item.description: The Swiss National Bank reported a solid six-month profit, as gains from the global stock-market rally and a weaker franc offset the drop in value of its gold holdings.

item.title: Murata Warns AI Spending Will Level Off After Raising Outlook
item.description: Murata Manufacturing Co. warned that the global technology buildout will eventually lose steam even as the maker of high-end AI components raised its profit outlook.
